quick_skim.title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation
quick_skim.abstract: We introduce EgoDepth-Bench, comprising 941,233 synchronized samples collected across 37 distinct physical environments. Each sample combines six calibrated RGB views with metric depth in the native fisheye view, reconstructed from five active-infrared stereo modules. A calibrated ball-bar confirms millimeter-level geometric accuracy, with a median error of 1.27 mm on a known sphere spacing. Environment-held-out splits enable evaluation of generalization to unseen environments. Across monocular, stereo, and multi-view models, the benchmark measures both depth accuracy and prediction coverage, including on hands and objects. Fine-tuning MapAnything on EgoDepth-Bench reduces metric AbsRel from 0.708 to 0.091 and scale-aligned AbsRel from 0.327 to 0.072 on unseen environments. These results demonstrate that EgoDepth-Bench provides effective supervision and enables rigorous evaluation of metric and relative depth estimation in egocentric manipulation. The project page provides the evaluation code and interactive RGB-depth sequences.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 第一人称操作场景缺少高精度度量深度评测基准，现有深度模型在真实环境中的精度与覆盖度难以衡量。作者构建EgoDepth-Bench，用五个主动红外双目模块重建鱼眼视角度量深度，汇集37个环境、94万余同步样本，并设置环境留出划分以测试泛化。校准球杆验证中位误差仅1.27毫米，微调MapAnything后度量AbsRel从0.708降至0.091。该基准可系统评估单目、双目与多视图模型的深度精度及手部物体覆盖，推动真实世界度量深度研究。

quick_skim.title: Segment Anything In-Context via Visual Demonstrations
quick_skim.abstract: We present the Segment Anything Model via Visual Demonstrations (SAYD), a foundation model for in-context segmentation. Given visual demos comprising prompt images and their segmentation masks, SAYD segments coherent regions (e.g., objects or their parts) in a query image by establishing visual correspondences between the prompts and the query. SAYD generalizes to previously-unseen segmentation tasks, including those requiring tacit visual knowledge or involving concepts that are difficult to articulate unambiguously in language. We train SAYD on 12 public datasets originally curated for panoptic segmentation using our proposed techniques, including a lightweight mask decoder for prompt-agnostic mask generation and a learning mechanism for recognizing novel query classes absent in the prompts. These innovations enhance both computational efficiency and out-of-domain generalization. Consequently, SAYD significantly outperforms existing methods of in-context segmentation and open-vocabulary segmentation across 24 out-of-domain benchmarks, spanning natural, biological, ecological, cosmological, medical, pathological, and satellite imagery.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有分割模型难以处理难以用语言明确表述的目标，也难以泛化到未见的分割任务。作者提出SAYD上下文分割基础模型，输入带掩码的提示图像，通过建立提示与查询图像间的视觉对应关系来分割查询图中的连贯区域。模型在12个全景分割数据集上训练，采用轻量掩码解码器与新颖类别识别机制。实验表明其可泛化到需默会视觉知识的未知分割任务，为开放式目标分割提供通用范式。

quick_skim.title: BridgeMVS: Bridging Multi-View Stereo and Monodepth via Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion
quick_skim.abstract: Multi-View Stereo (MVS) and Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) provide complementary cues for dense 3D reconstruction. While MVS leverages explicit geometry for metric depth, it struggles in challenging regions where feature matching is unreliable. Conversely, MDE provides robust structural priors but typically yields scale-ambiguous results. Existing hybrid methods mainly exploit monocular cues in a unidirectional manner, leaving the mutual enhancement between MDE and MVS insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose BridgeMVS, a unified cascaded multi-stage MVS framework that bridges monocular depth features and multi-view cost volume representations through Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion (BDF). At each stage, BDF performs dynamic mono-to-cost and cost-to-mono updates, where monocular structural features guide cost volume refinement for more robust MVS depth estimation, while multi-view geometric evidence recalibrates monocular representations to improve their metric-scale consistency. Furthermore, the fused monocular and multi-view representations are progressively propagated from coarse to fine stages and constrained by stage-wise relative-scale MDE supervision and metric-scale MVS supervision, enabling cross-branch interactions to benefit subsequent high-resolution depth estimation. In addition, BDF is designed as a plug-and-play module that can be conveniently integrated into existing cascaded MVS frameworks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BridgeMVS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DTU, Tanks-and-Temples, and ETH3D benchmarks, while simultaneously boosting the accuracy of monocular depth estimation. Notably, BridgeMVS ranks first on both the Tanks-and-Temples Intermediate and Advanced benchmarks. The source code is available at \href{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 多视图立体在弱纹理区域匹配不可靠，而单目深度估计虽提供稳健结构先验却存在尺度模糊。本文提出BridgeMVS级联多阶段框架，通过双向动态融合模块在各阶段交互单目深度特征与多视图代价体表示。实验表明该融合能互补两类线索，提升稠密重建的精度与鲁棒性，为MVS与单目深度的相互增强提供了新思路。
